reading: The Polish Aviation Museum in Kraków preserves and interprets aviation on the former Rakowice-Czyżyny airfield. Its collection spans aircraft, gliders, helicopters and engines, alongside archives, models and surviving fragments; its exhibitions range from early flight and civil aviation to military and Cold War aircraft. It treats aviation as a story of makers, pilots, clubs, service and communities as well as machines, and actively restores overlooked histories, including women's contributions. Education is hands-on: flight physics, model building, art, guided routes and family events sit beside preservation and historical research. Its vocabulary is tactile and aeronautical: hangars, wings, airfields, exhibits, collections, gliders, engines, flight paths, upwind and downwind. What makes this place distinctive is the overlap of a real historic runway, a vast collection, seven interwoven civil-flight themes, damaged objects kept as they survived, and the miniature aircraft built by visitors. The swarm can exploit the tension between preserving the past and teaching people to make something new.

enemies.idea: Akar replicas compete to be the first glider airborne, fastening towlines to anything that moves and dragging it toward a launch point.
enemies.why: The first-flight contest turns a quiet approach into a contest over who controls the towline.

enemies.idea: Wrona and Żaba gliders hunt as a pair: one circles overhead while the other waits on the ground, exchanging their roles whenever the wind shifts.
enemies.why: The crow and frog names suggest complementary aerial and ground tactics, with a readable wind-driven opening.

enemies.idea: A corrupted aerobatics machine loops around a fixed centre, leaving hard ribbons of disturbed air that turn a straight run into a rolling obstacle course.
enemies.why: The Zlin aerobatics display becomes a spatial puzzle whose dangerous pattern can be learned.

enemies.idea: A model workshop's radio-controlled scouts steal loose parts and assemble larger copies of themselves, but a recovered transmitter can scramble their formation.
enemies.why: Their growth gives the crew a reason to interrupt construction and a tangible tool to turn against them.

enemies.idea: Aerolaboratory demonstrators test lift on everything they meet: paired fans raise a target while a third machine removes its footholds.
enemies.why: A lesson in flight physics becomes a coordinated trap with fans that can be redirected.

enemies.idea: Wood, cardboard and plastic model-builders each repair their own kind: saws harvest struts, shears cut skins and heated nozzles weld joints.
enemies.why: Three workshop materials produce different vulnerabilities and force a choice of which repairer to stop first.

enemies.idea: A storeroom of surviving aircraft fragments walks on mismatched spars, refusing to be made whole and collecting other machines' broken parts as armor.
enemies.why: The museum's choice to preserve damaged objects becomes a scavenger whose defenses change during a fight.

enemies.idea: A Metamuseum collector builds a miniature museum inside its own frame, deploying tiny aircraft to retrieve anything it considers a missing exhibit.
enemies.why: The collection's history and model-making fold into a nested encounter: disabling the collector also releases its small fleet.

enemies.idea: Cold War hangar sentries treat the route as two rival airspaces and repeatedly shift the dividing line, catching anyone stranded on the wrong side.
enemies.why: A moving boundary turns the hangar into a positioning challenge without reenacting a real battle.

enemies.idea: The engine collection has become a choir of starter motors; each unit spins faster when another is silenced, unless their fuel lines are interrupted together.
enemies.why: Over 130 engines inspire a chain-reaction encounter that rewards coordination over simply attacking the loudest one.

enemies.idea: Helicopter scavengers hover over a prize and use their rotor wash to scatter the crew's equipment before swooping down to take it.
enemies.why: Rotor wash makes the surroundings and dropped gear matter before the machines commit to close range.

enemies.idea: An unpowered glider pack waits for warm air rising from working engines, then silently dives through the draft at anyone who shut one down.
enemies.why: An enemy's route is visible in the air currents, and the crew can alter it by managing heat sources.

enemies.idea: A runway kite swarm tangles its long lines into a shifting net; its brightly colored sails reveal which strand is bearing the load.
enemies.why: The festival's joyful silhouettes become a wind-driven snare that can be unpicked rather than merely smashed.

enemies.idea: A jury of drawing machines tries to make every flying thing match a winning picture, projecting outlines that constrain anyone caught inside them.
enemies.why: The young creators' flight-art competition becomes a fight over imaginative variation versus enforced sameness.

enemies.idea: A route marshal sorts intruders into civil and military tours, then sends moving barriers to prevent anyone from crossing between the two paths.
enemies.why: Two real tour themes become a navigable maze; switching classifications opens one route and closes another.

enemies.idea: An overzealous preservation trolley seals moving objects in padded clamps, mistaking the crew for fragile exhibits that must never be touched.
enemies.why: Its protective purpose creates a nonlethal but escalating threat, and careful handling can fool it.

enemies.idea: A supersonic timetable runner races a fixed imaginary passenger route, generating a pressure pulse each time it reaches a scheduled waypoint.
enemies.why: The first scheduled Tu-144 service becomes a predictable high-speed hazard with safe gaps between passes.

enemies.idea: An amateur aircraft assembled from basic tools keeps changing its own shape mid-pursuit, borrowing whatever implements it finds to rebuild its wings.
enemies.why: The J-2B Polonez story of 800 hours and basic tools inspires a resourceful opponent whose next form depends on the room.

enemies.idea: A birthday puzzle constructor locks its prize inside three nested flying models; each incorrect assembly sends another small decoy buzzing away with a component.
enemies.why: The flying riddle and aviation constructors packages become a playful assembly challenge under pressure.

enemies.idea: An airfield surveyor extends phantom runway markings across the old grounds, ordering machines and people to clear a strip that keeps changing direction.
enemies.why: The former airfield's history shapes a battlefield where painted lines telegraph the next dangerous approach.

enemies.idea: An archive scanner mistakes shadows for missing records and pins them flat with sweeping beams, immobilizing whoever casts them until the light is interrupted.
enemies.why: Archive digitization becomes a light-and-cover puzzle grounded in the museum's work of recording its holdings.

enemies.idea: A collection counter releases a small retrieval drone whenever an aircraft leaves its assigned place; it cannot distinguish a rescue from a theft.
enemies.why: The collection of over 189 aircraft becomes a pressure mechanic for moving a needed machine out of the hangar.

allies.idea: A surviving model-maker can build an unpowered decoy from scraps and teach the crew to fly it past the radio-controlled scouts.
allies.why: A practical skill from the workshop gives the crew an inventive way to redirect the swarm.

allies.idea: An accessibility guide knows the quiet hours, induction loop and refuge points, and can lead a group through the museum using sound, touch or simple directions as needed.
allies.why: The museum's actual commitment to different ways of visiting becomes a reliable network of routes and communication.

allies.idea: A conservation team protects unrestored fragments and can identify which broken spar is original and which is a swarm component pretending to belong.
allies.why: Their knowledge makes careful observation valuable and keeps damaged artifacts from being treated as disposable loot.

allies.idea: A volunteer guide knows both the civil-aviation and military-history routes and can switch the crew between them at a safe junction.
allies.why: Knowledge of the museum's distinct routes becomes a concrete advantage against the route marshal.

allies.idea: A small crew of young artists folds vivid paper gliders that carry messages through narrow spaces beyond the swarm's reach.
allies.why: The creativity celebrated by the competition remains useful and hopeful in the occupied museum.

bosses.idea: The Curator of Perfect Flight has fused seven civil-aviation zones into one enormous flying collection. It switches between glider towlines, aerobatic air ribbons and service-aircraft retrieval arms, trying to make every machine fit a single ideal of flight. Each freed zone removes one of its capabilities.
bosses.why: The seven overlapping themes become a many-stage encounter about the museum's diversity, with a clear payoff for rescuing each section.

bosses.idea: The Airfield That Remembers is a runway-length machine built from surveyors, engine banks and miniature aircraft. It tries to freeze the former airfield at one moment forever, repeatedly launching its models along freshly drawn paths. The crew can interrupt its cycle by restoring the signals for departure and return at opposite ends.
bosses.why: The site as historic airfield, collection and living place becomes a boss whose whole landscape is part of the encounter.

bosses.idea: The Museum of One Model is a vast nested collector that copies the whole collection at smaller and smaller scales, absorbing real objects to perfect its miniature. Its own tiny exhibits can be released to jam the machinery that builds them.
bosses.why: The museum's origins and model-making combine into a self-referential finale with a satisfying reversal.

events.idea: A kite line has snagged a runway marker and the changing wind is drawing a net across a safe crossing. The crew can wait for a lull or free the marker without tearing the sail.
events.why: A small wind-reading problem makes the festival setting interactive.

events.idea: A cardboard model glides out of a workshop carrying a hand-drawn map, then catches a thermal above an engine. Catch it or cool the engine to retrieve the message.
events.why: A lesson in materials and lift creates a gentle chase with two practical solutions.

events.idea: A preserved fragment and a swarm-made replica have been mixed together. A conservator asks the crew to compare wear and fittings before either piece is moved.
events.why: The distinction between an authentic surviving object and a reconstruction becomes a meaningful choice.

events.idea: A glider towline stretches across a corridor, slowly pulling a supply cart toward a launch. Releasing the tension safely leaves both the supplies and the fragile model intact.
events.why: A flight mechanism creates a compact rescue problem with something worth preserving.

events.idea: A guide's civil and military routes have been spliced together by the swarm. Choosing a junction correctly gets a stranded group to the new hangar before the barriers reset.
events.why: The tour routes provide a quick navigation challenge with visible consequences.

events.idea: A quiet refuge is losing its power to a noisy engine bank. The crew can reroute the supply and give the people sheltering there a calm way to communicate again.
events.why: Protecting an accessible refuge gives a practical, human goal to an engine-room detour.

events.idea: Two radio-controlled models circle over a workbench, each carrying half a transmitter. The crew can lure them to land by placing the correct spare parts on the bench.
events.why: The RC workshop becomes a low-stakes negotiation with machines that want materials.

events.idea: An aerobatic aircraft keeps drawing a loop in the air above a misplaced trophy. The crew must time a dash into the centre to recover it between passes.
events.why: The display's aerobatics and trophies combine into a clear timing challenge.

events.idea: A miniature exhibition inside the Metamuseum is missing its tiny hangar. Returning the piece reveals a hidden compartment with a hand-built escape glider.
events.why: The model-making theme rewards attention to scale and careful reconstruction.

events.idea: A birthday flying-riddle kit has scattered its pieces through a room. Solving the simple assembly lets the finished model carry a cord over a locked gate.
events.why: A children's activity becomes a useful, playful tool for the crew.

events.idea: The crew finds a stack of imaginative flight drawings being sorted into identical piles by a machine. Save the varied designs before it cuts them to one pattern.
events.why: Protecting individual creativity gives the swarm's obsession with uniformity a concrete cost.

events.idea: A cluster of old airfield markers points in conflicting directions. Aligning them with the remaining runway markings reveals a safe way across the grounds.
events.why: The former airfield becomes a navigational clue rather than generic scenery.

events.idea: A family workshop's winter experiments have left a pane frosted over; a warm airflow from a nearby fan reveals a route sketched on the other side.
events.why: Winter experimentation and airflow create a small environmental discovery.

events.idea: A supersonic timetable machine demands a departure on a route no longer usable. Give it a new closed circuit and it clears a corridor while rehearsing the schedule.
events.why: The scheduled-flight detail offers a way to solve an encounter by satisfying the machine's routine.
